provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for summer: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 青田 ao-ta (#85A761), then 夏影 natsu-kage (#4E8164), then 木漏日 ko-more-bi (#DBD591), then 夏空 natsu-zora (#5DA8D3). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 17.6, 32.8, 44.3 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: Four summer-tagged entries, read as a field under a sky: the paddy green (青田) outermost, its shade (夏影) beneath, dappled light (木漏日) where the layers part, and the summer sky (夏空) as the innermost edge. Every member carries the summer tag, so this is the most seasonally unmixed layering in the set. The name is ours (夏野, "Summer Field"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
